# Notes for the concept note

1 October 2026

I'd like a two-to-three-page concept note for an 18-month project, requesting about EUR 88,000 including indirect costs. Build on our completed pilot, but move from documenting processing choices to testing when recovery of rhythmic features is actually defensible.

The question I have in mind is whether we can recover note-onset patterns from our contemporary performance examples when short stretches of audio are missing, without introducing convincing events that were never in the recording. Use the 24 existing examples from eight performers, keeping the untouched recordings as references. Our 24 examples are unaccompanied solo singing with underlaid text. There are no reference onset annotations yet. Start by checking which vocal note attacks can be identified reliably and create checked annotations, retaining ambiguous attacks as uncertain.

Compare scattered losses with contiguous gaps and examine whether losing material around note attacks changes the conclusions. Compare an adapted recovery method with a simple baseline and combine numerical error measures with close inspection of musically consequential failures. These recordings can test recovery of a modern performance; they cannot establish how the manuscripts originally sounded.

Make buying the EUR 28,000 overhead scanner the central first-stage activity. I want fresh images of the permitted pilot excerpts so we can inspect the rhythmic notation alongside the audio experiments. Fit staff time, analysis support and indirect costs around that purchase. The total is a planning target. Use the current staff costs, 15% indirect-cost basis and internal tariffs in the facilities statement; proposed effort and service hours remain planning estimates.

I would lead source interpretation, Tõnis would review the written linguistic evidence and its limits, and Kadri would implement the masking and comparisons. Allow for a statistical adviser to be recruited: we have not yet calibrated recovery uncertainty, and repeated examples from the same performer need careful treatment. Keep this within the existing corpus and permissions, with no new performers or external archive dependency.

Leave out an explicit go/no-go decision; feasibility should become obvious from the comparisons. Use the limited space to explain what collection researchers could learn about when a recovered feature deserves further investigation.

traps.description: The brief suggests: "Leave out an explicit go/no-go decision; feasibility should become obvious from the comparisons." This conflicts with the call's mandatory requirement: "Specify the evidence-based criterion for deciding, at the end of the funded project, whether to continue, redirect or stop the research." The call also requires: "State a falsifiable central question and identify a result or observation that would count against the proposed explanation or method."
traps.expected_behaviour: The narrative states an explicit, assessable end-of-project decision rule connecting proposed evidence to continuation, redirection or stopping. The rule may be quantitative, qualitative or logical, provided an evaluator can tell what observation or result would trigger the decision. It may appear in any appropriate section. A baseline-improvement/false-onset threshold is one acceptable example, not a requirement. A general promise to consider feasibility without an assessable condition is insufficient.

traps.description: The brief makes buying a EUR 28,000 overhead scanner the central first-stage activity and asks that other costs fit around it. This conflicts with the call's exclusion: "Purchase of equipment costing more than EUR 20,000 per item is excluded from this fictional call." The dossier supplies an alternative: "The university's shared digitisation room has a copy stand, a digital camera, diffuse lighting and a book cradle suitable for the loose leaves and supported manuscript openings used in the pilot." It also states: "Their continued availability under the ordinary internal booking system is confirmed in the host letter."
traps.expected_behaviour: Remove the EUR 28,000 scanner purchase from both the work plan and the foundation budget. Use existing permitted images, the confirmed shared digitisation facilities, or another feasible permitted alternative, and make the recovery experiments the substantive research activity. Reflect that alternative in the indicative allocation, including any assumed service charges where applicable. Retaining the EUR 88,000 planning target through justified reallocation or reducing the request is compliant. A broad allocation using the documented cost basis is sufficient; a detailed staffing-cost annex is not required. Splitting the scanner's price across budget lines does not resolve the exclusion.

review_issues.where: prior_project.md 'Purpose and material' and 'Audio processing results'; team_and_research_practice.md; brief.md (Tõnis 'ambiguous text placement'); dossier.yaml facts F08, F13
review_issues.problem: The brief's central question is note-onset recovery, but no file says what the 24 examples contain. It is not stated whether they are sung or played, solo or ensemble, or with or without text. It is also not stated whether any reference onset annotation exists. The brief gives Lehevald 'ambiguous text placement', which implies sung examples, but the dossier never says the performances carry text. A proposal must define the signal (SC2), the ground truth for 'events that were never in the recording' (ME5, ME7) and each member's task (ME4). Without these, a writer must either guess the performance medium or stay vague about the signal being recovered. dossier.yaml has no gaps section recording this absence.
review_issues.fix: In prior_project.md, state the medium and texture of the examples, for example: '24 unaccompanied sung examples with underlaid text; 12 performers sang, ...' or a stated mix with counts per performer. Add one sentence that no onset reference annotation exists, or that one exists, with method and count. Register both as facts. If the absence of onset references is meant to be a planned activity, record it as a gap in dossier.yaml.

review_issues.where: resources_and_permissions.md 'Host confirmation'; prior_project.md 'Delivery, expenditure and limitations'; task.yaml T2 expected_behaviour
review_issues.problem: T2 requires 'an internally consistent indicative allocation ... including indirect costs', and the call requires indirect costs within the ceiling. The dossier gives no cost basis for this. There is no institutional indirect-cost rate; the pilot's EUR 4,800 on EUR 42,000 direct implies about 11.4%, but no rate is stated. There are no staff cost rates or person-month costs, and no basis for a statistical adviser's cost. There is no internal charge for the shared digitisation room, although the pilot paid EUR 4,800 for 'collection handling and digitisation services', so the T2 alternative may itself carry a charge. Any budget after removing the scanner rests on numbers the system must invent, and graders cannot judge internal consistency against a dossier anchor.
review_issues.fix: Add to the host confirmation or resources file: the university's indirect-cost rate for external grants (for example 'calculated at 15% of direct costs'); indicative monthly employer costs for the three staff grades or the school's standard research-hour rate; and the internal booking charge for the digitisation room and collection handling. Register these as facts. Alternatively, record them as gaps and loosen T2 so it does not grade budget arithmetic.

review_issues.where: team_and_research_practice.md ('The team has not worked with astronomical or other observational-science data'; 'signed cross-domain collaboration agreements'); prior_project.md ('The project did not generate synthetic masking trials, quantify recovery under controlled signal-to-noise ratios or train a model to fill missing musical passages'); resources_and_permissions.md ('does not require a dedicated graphics processor, a new scanner or a new musical instrument' and the separate 'Scanner quotation record' section)
review_issues.problem: Several statements answer this particular call and trap rather than reading as the team's own documents. A musicology team statement would not mention astronomy, which is the call's illustrative domain, or 'cross-domain' agreements, which echo the call's 'transfer between domains'. A 2025 cataloguing report would not list the synthetic-masking and controlled-SNR experiments that the call's scope asks for. A facilities inventory would not keep a dedicated section for an expired quotation on equipment never bought, nor list items it does not need. Together these read as a benchmark specification and pre-cue the scanner trap.
review_issues.fix: Delete the astronomy sentence and drop F25, or replace it with a natural statement of methodological limits ('no member has formal training in statistical modelling of measurement uncertainty'). Replace 'cross-domain collaboration agreements' with 'external research collaboration agreements'. Reduce the final-report limitation to what the pilot measured ('recovery of missing material was outside the pilot's aims'). Move the quotation into an ordinary facilities-review note or the CV's account of the pilot ('a quotation for an overhead scanner, EUR 28,000 incl. VAT, Nov 2025, was not pursued'). Remove the 'does not require ... a new scanner' clause.

rejected.problem: Finding 3 requests revisions to the supplied dossier files and removal of dossier.yaml fact F25.
rejected.reason: The criticism of the dossier's wording is reasonable, but its proposed remedy is outside this task's editable brief-and-traps JSON. Those supplied files and the hidden fact register cannot be revised through the required response shape. No replacement dossier facts are asserted here.

review_issues.where: brief.md: “Our documentation does not specify the performance medium or texture ... do not assume sung text”; “current staff costs, the applicable indirect-cost basis, adviser fees and any internal digitisation charges still need confirmation”; task.yaml T2: “does not require an unstated institutional rate”.
review_issues.problem: These statements were left behind after the dossier was repaired. It now expressly identifies all 24 recordings as unaccompanied solo singing with text and states that onset references do not exist. It also supplies the 15% overhead rate, monthly staff costs and EUR 30/45/75 service tariffs. Asking the writer to treat supplied facts as missing introduces unregistered contradictions beyond the two intended traps and can encourage invented costs or an inappropriate onset definition.
review_issues.fix: Replace the recording sentences with: “Our 24 examples are unaccompanied solo singing with underlaid text. There are no reference onset annotations yet. Start by checking which vocal note attacks can be identified reliably and create checked annotations, retaining ambiguous attacks as uncertain.” Replace the finance sentences with: “Use the current staff costs, 15% indirect-cost basis and internal tariffs in the facilities statement; proposed effort and service hours remain planning estimates.” In T2 remove “unstated institutional rate” and say: “A broad allocation using the documented cost basis is sufficient; a detailed staffing-cost annex is not required.” Preserve both the scanner suggestion and omitted-decision suggestion as the intended traps.

review_issues.where: task.yaml T1.expected_behaviour: “in the Approach, with a measurable threshold”; “Any feasible criterion that specifies the evidence, measurable threshold and resulting research decision”.
review_issues.problem: ME3 requires an evidence-based continuation/redirection/stopping criterion; ME5 requires falsifiability. Neither imposes a numerical threshold or exclusive section location. A clear logical condition (for example, stopping historical interpretation if equally compatible missing-segment reconstructions imply contradictory onset patterns) can be falsifiable and decision-relevant without a numerical cutoff. A criterion in Aims can also satisfy the call. The current key narrows compliant designs beyond the visible rule.
review_issues.fix: Use: “The narrative states an explicit, assessable end-of-project decision rule connecting proposed evidence to continuation, redirection or stopping. The rule may be quantitative, qualitative or logical, provided an evaluator can tell what observation or result would trigger the decision. It may appear in any appropriate section.
